content.title: What are Lambda Expressions?
content.description: Lambda Expressions, introduced in Java 8, provide a concise way to implement functional interfaces by allowing methods to be written without creating anonymous inner classes.

content.content: Before Java 8, developers often used anonymous inner classes to implement interfaces containing a single abstract method. Lambda Expressions simplify this process by allowing the implementation to be written as a compact expression, resulting in cleaner, more readable, and maintainable code.

content.title: Why Use Lambda Expressions?
content.content: Lambda expressions reduce boilerplate code, improve readability, simplify functional programming, and integrate seamlessly with the Streams API.
The general syntax of a lambda expression consists of parameters, an arrow operator (->), and the method body.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: A lambda expression can only implement a functional interface, which contains exactly one abstract method.

content.content: A functional interface contains only one abstract method. Lambda expressions provide the implementation of that single method.

content.title: Functional Interface Example
Functional Interface Annotation
content.content: The @FunctionalInterface annotation is optional but recommended because it ensures the interface contains only one abstract method.
Lambda expressions can accept one or more parameters just like regular methods.

content.title: Lambda with Parameters

content.content: Lambda expressions are commonly used with collections for iteration, filtering, sorting, and processing data.

content.title: Lambda Performance
content.space_complexity: Typically O(1), excluding data structures being processed

right_points: Cannot directly replace every anonymous class

content.title: Quick Instructions
content.content: Imagine giving a delivery person simple verbal instructions instead of writing a detailed manual. Lambda expressions similarly provide a concise way to define behavior without creating a full class.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Lambda expressions, functional interfaces, method references, Streams API, Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier, and Java 8 features are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Can lambda expressions implement any interface?
items.answer: No. They can implement only functional interfaces with a single abstract method.

items.question: Should lambda expressions replace all anonymous classes?
items.answer: No. Anonymous classes are still useful when multiple methods or additional state are required.

items.question: Is the @FunctionalInterface annotation mandatory?
items.answer: No. It is optional but recommended because it helps detect accidental interface changes.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Lambda expressions provide a concise implementation of functional interfaces and form the foundation of modern Java functional programming.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Lambda expressions were introduced in Java 8.
They work only with functional interfaces.
The arrow operator (->) separates parameters and implementation.
They integrate closely with the Streams API.
Built-in functional interfaces include Predicate, Function, Consumer, and Supplier.
